page: Amazon Web Services c7gd.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the arm64 architecture, it features 64 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 microarchitecture running at 2.6 GHz. The server is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It includes 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps, operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data highlights strong multi-core performance and memory efficiency. The c7gd.16xlarge achieves top-tier results in multi-core Geekbench tests and software compilation with Clang. Its memory subsystem demonstrates high read and write bandwidth, scoring in the top tier of Passmark memory benchmarks. Multi-core CPU performance under stress-ng and CPU physics simulations are also strong. Single-core performance, including Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core tests, falls within the average range.

Given its compute-focused architecture and high-capacity local NVMe SSD storage, the c7gd.16xlarge is well-suited for workloads requiring high-speed local data access and parallel processing. These include database operations, software compilation, static web serving, and multi-threaded decompression tasks. The custom ARM-based Graviton processor provides high resource density and compute efficiency relative to its hardware profile, making it a viable option for scale-out workloads that benefit from dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading.
